thread:
anya: Heads-up — seeing a regression on dedicated pool eu-west-2-pool-7 after last runtime deploy. Token p50 up ~12%, p95 widened. Not across all pools, mostly heavy chat routes.
ops-bot: Alert: pool_latency_spike eu-west-2-pool-7 — p95_tokens +45ms, triggered at 1810054300.
mike: Same here. Replayed some traces — kernel_select is often choosing fallback_generic for short seqs (~<64) which increases per-token overhead.
cheng: Ran a sampling profile (10k requests) and exported runtime counters. Short summary: 
```
kernel_choice: {optimized_matmul: 62%, fallback_generic: 31%, quant_kern: 7%}
batch_fill_pct: median 34% (route chat-stream), kv_cache_local_hit: 68% -> dropped from 83% pre-deploy
avg_tokens_per_batch: 4.1 -> used to be 6.8
```
Notably fallback_generic has ~1.8x longer per-token latency in our bench.
ellie: KV cache hit drop aligns with more small batches — less prefix reuse. Are batching heuristics changed in the latest canary?
samir: Yes — I adjusted max_wait_ms from 12->4 to reduce tail lat, but it lowered batch fill and probably killed kvcache reuse. The idea was to favor latency for chat, but it's backfiring because kernel dispatch cost goes up.
anya: That makes sense. We need better metrics to connect kernel selection, batching behavior, and kv hits per route + per pool. Current dashboards are too coarse.
mike: Agreed. Proposal for new instruments/metrics: 
- runtime.kernel_choice{pool,model,route,choice} counter per-token
- runtime.batch_fill_pct{pool,route} gauge sampled per-batch
- runtime.kv_cache_local_hits / runtime.kv_cache_local_requests labels: pool,route,model
- runtime.pool_headroom_tokens gauge (remaining tokens before saturation)
- runtime.pool_latency_stddev histogram per-pool for noisy-neighbor detection

Add a small sampled flamegraph label: runtime.prof_tag per-request for rolling samples.
cheng: Also add derived KPIs in dashboards: p50/p95 per-token broken down by kernel_choice, and p50_by_batch_size. Quick PromQL sketches: 
```
# kernel split p95
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,kernel_choice,pool,route))
# kv cache hit rate per route
sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_local_hits[5m])) by (route,pool) / sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_local_requests[5m])) by (route,pool)
# pool headroom
avg(runtime_pool_capacity_tokens - runtime_pool_inflight_tokens) by (pool) / runtime_pool_capacity_tokens
```
samir: For noisy-neighbor detection, we should alert on: pool_latency_stddev > 30ms AND batch_fill_pct < 40% sustained for 5m. That catches contention vs workload change.
ellie: Can we add a panel that shows route->pool routing heatmap so we can see if a specific route is dumping cheap short requests on a pool optimized for long-context kernels?
anya: Yes. Also add a per-route knob: prefer_low_latency boolean that toggles batching heuristic per-route. We'll test toggling for affected routes.
mike: Quick mitigation plan: roll back batching change for eu-west-2-pool-7 canary (reduce aggressiveness), enable more aggressive kernel selection policy (prefer optimized_matmul for short seqs if model compatibility check passes), and increase kvcache window to reduce eviction for short sessions.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for runtime-canary eu-west-2 at 1810054420 by mike. Canary traffic set 10% -> 0%.
cheng: I pushed a small instrumentation patch to emit runtime.kernel_choice and batch_fill_pct (sampling 1/100 requests to limit cardinality). Patch: 
```
# runtime config snippet
metrics_sampling:
  kernel_choice: 0.01
  batch_fill_pct: 0.01
```
Will follow up with dashboards.
samir: I'll revert the max_wait_ms change in canary and observe. If headroom recovers and kv hit rate + kernel_choice mix move back, we can roll forward with different knobs.
anya: Can someone add panels: per-pool headroom gauge, kernel_choice breakdown stacked bar (by route), kv_cache_hit_rate heatmap by route, and noisy-neighbor alert rule? Put them under "Dedicated -> Pools -> eu-west-2-pool-7".
ellie: I'll make the dashboard and create a helper link to route->pool mapping. Also adding a p95_by_kernel panel and a small note: "do not use p95 alone; look at per-token and per-batch context".
mike: After rollback, watch the same route traces and post new profile. If p95 drops and kernel_choice optimized_matmul increases back to ~70%, then change validated.
anya: TL;DR: regression traced to batching heuristic + kernel selection interaction causing lower batch_fill -> lower kvcache hit -> more fallback kernels -> higher per-token latency. Mitigations: rollback batching tweak in canary, emit new metrics (kernel_choice, batch_fill_pct, kv cache rates), add dashboards and alerts for pool headroom and noisy neighbors. Owners: cheng (metrics), ellie (dashboards), samir (canary revert), mike (rollback + verification).
ops-bot: Note: incident ticket INC-2026-224 created for follow-up and postmortem.
anya: Thanks team — let's sync in 30m if the rollback doesn't stabilize.
